tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch a URL and return its content as clean markdown. Handles Twitter/X tweets, YouTube videos (with transcripts), arXiv papers, PDFs, Wikipedia articles, and GitHub repos/files/issues/PRs/releases directly. Direct image URLs (png/jpeg/gif/webp) are returned as an image block for vision. Otherwise checks a shared cache, then falls back through a multi-tier chain: Jina Reader, web archives (Wayback, archive.ph, Arquivo.pt), raw fetch, RSS, CrossRef, Semantic Scholar, HackerNews, Reddit, OG meta. Long pages are truncated at maxLength characters — paginate with startIndex. Results are cached for the session; pass noCache to force a live fetch.

maxTier.description: Stop at this tier (1-5, default 5). Lower = faster but fewer fallbacks.

startIndex.description: Character offset to start from, for paginating long content (default 0)

noCache.description: Skip session and shared caches and fetch live content

tools.name: fetch_batch
tools.description: Fetch up to 10 URLs in parallel and return each as clean markdown. Same handler/fallback chain as the fetch tool, with a smaller per-URL length budget. Use after a search to pull several sources in one call.

maxTier.description: Stop at this tier (1-5, default 5). Lower = faster but fewer fallbacks.

maxLength.description: Maximum characters to return per URL (default 20000)

noCache.description: Skip session and shared caches and fetch live content

tools.name: research
tools.description: Search the web and fetch the content of the top results in one call. Returns the full content of each result as markdown, ready to summarize or compare. Use this instead of separate search + fetch calls when researching a topic.

count.description: Number of top results to fetch (1-5, default 3)

maxLength.description: Maximum characters to return per result (default 20000)

site.description: Restrict results to a domain, e.g. "docs.python.org"

freshness.description: Only return results from the last day/week/month/year (ignored by the DuckDuckGo fallback)

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the web and return results. Uses Brave Search API if BRAVE_API_KEY is set, otherwise falls back to SearXNG and then DuckDuckGo. Supports domain filtering (site), freshness, and pagination (page).

site.description: Restrict results to a domain, e.g. "github.com"

freshness.description: Only return results from the last day/week/month/year (ignored by the DuckDuckGo fallback)

page.description: 1-based results page for pagination (default 1; ignored by the DuckDuckGo fallback)

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Extract specific values from a web page as JSON instead of markdown prose. Provide CSS selectors to pull named fields (text or an attribute, first match or all), and/or set tables:true to convert every HTML table to arrays of row objects. Use this when you need particular data (prices, lists, specs, tabular data) rather than the whole page. Honors per-domain auth and proxies.

selectors.description: Map of field name to CSS selector, e.g. {"title":"h1","price":".price","links":{"selector":"a.item","attr":"href","all":true}}

attr.description: Extract this attribute (e.g. href, src) instead of text

all.description: Return every match as an array instead of the first

tables.description: Extract all HTML tables as arrays of row objects (default true when no selectors are given)
